lesson_title: Magnetic Declination: The Compass That Tells a Small Lie
hook_text: Your compass lies to you — by a known angle that grows every year. The exam pays you to measure the lie.
clip_script: Hold an imaginary compass flat in your hand. The map on the table points at true north — the top of the world, the fixed pole all maps agree on. But the needle in your hand ignores the map and swings to its own north, the magnetic one, which in South Africa sits off to the west. Two arrows, two norths, and a wedge of angle between them. That wedge is magnetic declination: the size of the compass's lie. And the lie is not even loyal — the magnetic pole wanders, so the wedge widens by a few minutes every year.
visual_style: Split view of a topographic map arrow and a compass needle slowly diverging, the wedge between them glowing and ticking wider year by year with a date counter.
pacing: Whispered hook, steady reveal of the wedge, date counter accelerating to the finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and update the lie to this year in four moves.
